title: Merge API key input into start screen
story: As a user, I want to enter my API key on the same screen where I start the exercise so that there are fewer steps to get started.
acceptance_criteria: The separate API key screen is removed — the app no longer shows ApiKeyForm as a standalone step
The start screen includes an API key input field of type password
The Start button is disabled when the API key field is empty
The Start button is enabled when the API key field has a non-empty value
The API key is held in React state for the session only — cleared on page refresh, never written to localStorage
The API key is passed into the exercise flow on Start
Unit tests cover: disabled state when empty, enabled state when filled, key passed on start

title: Auto-growing editor with no resize handle
story: As a user, I want the editor to grow and shrink vertically as I type so that I can focus on my writing without a visible resize handle.
acceptance_criteria: The resize handle is not visible on the editor
The editor height increases as text is added beyond the current height
The editor height decreases as text is removed
The editor does not grow horizontally
A minimum height is set so the editor is not zero-height when empty
Unit tests cover: resize handle absent, height grows when content exceeds current height, height shrinks when content is removed

title: Consistent premium styling across all screens
story: As a user, I want the app to have a consistent, minimal look and feel inspired by iA Writer so that it feels like a premium writing tool rather than an unstyled form.
acceptance_criteria: No browser-default button or form element styles are visible on any screen
All screens share a single centered content container with a consistent max-width
On viewports narrower than the max-width, the layout fills the screen with comfortable horizontal padding
On viewports wider than the max-width, content is centered and does not stretch edge-to-edge
The writing textarea spans the full width of the content container
The writing textarea uses a font size comfortable for extended writing (larger than browser default)
The highlighted results text is constrained to the content container width
Typography, spacing, and color palette are consistent across all screens and reference iA Writer's aesthetic: monospace or serif font, neutral colors, generous whitespace
A Storybook story exists (or is updated) for each screen showing the styled result, with written instructions in the story for how a human reviewer can validate the visual appearance

title: Highlights snap to word boundaries
agent_retro: After the plan changed mid-execution (user corrected the root cause analysis), I proceeded directly into implementation without re-confirming the updated plan with the user.
user_retro: Agent went directly into executing before getting confirmation that the plan was acceptable. Also, marking tasks as in-progress has no value when only one agent is running at a time. Agent should not read the codebase while writing stories.
story: As a user, I want sensory highlights to cover only complete words so that partial-word highlights don't appear in the results.
acceptance_criteria: Highlights always start at the first character of a word — leading punctuation or partial characters before the first word are excluded
Highlights always end at the last character of the final word in the phrase — trailing punctuation after the last word is excluded
Punctuation between highlighted words (e.g. a comma in 'feathered, fuzzy') is included in the highlight
Multi-word phrases are highlighted in full from the first word boundary to the last
Overlapping annotations are out of scope
Tests cover: partial-word start trimmed, trailing punctuation trimmed, inter-word punctuation retained, multi-word phrase fully highlighted
